transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. Well, I came in because for the past few weeks, I’ve just felt this... this really heavy, sad pressure sitting on me almost all day. It's exhausting because I'm a nurse, an LPN, so I have to be at work smiling at patients all shift, but inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together. 

Speaking of my patients, I actually had this one gentleman yesterday, Mr. Davis, who was telling me all about his grandson's travel baseball tournament. They drove all the way down to Florida for it. I've only been to Florida once, when I was like ten, for Disney World. I remember it was so incredibly humid my hair was just a giant frizz ball the entire trip. My mom kept trying to put it in these tight French braids to keep it out of my face, but I hated sitting still for it... 

Wait, what was I saying? Um, I'm sorry. Yeah, just... that heavy, sad feeling. I'm just really struggling to keep it together lately.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you normally like to do, or has that changed recently?

Yeah, it’s... it's definitely changed. After my shifts, I used to do a lot of things to decompress. I’d paint, or go to yoga, or go to this salsa class downtown. I actually bought these amazing silver shoes for salsa. They have this little strappy part around the ankle that makes them feel super secure when you spin. I found them at a thrift store for like eight bucks, which is crazy because thrift stores are getting so expensive lately. Have you noticed that? Like, they price used, faded sweaters at twenty dollars now. My roommate, Sarah, buys almost all her clothes there, and she was just complaining the other day about how they mark up the vintage stuff... 

Wait, sorry, I'm rambling again. Um, what I meant was... I don't really use the shoes or go to the classes anymore. Lately, I just go straight home, sit on the couch, and ignore all my texts. It just... none of it feels worth the effort right now.
Do you still find pleasure in the things you're doing, even if it's just a little bit?

Not really. Not even a little bit. I mean, I try to. The other morning before my shift, I stopped at this bakery near the clinic to get a blueberry muffin. I usually love them. The lady who runs the place is so sweet, she always asks about my work. She actually just had a grandbaby, a little girl. She was showing me pictures on her phone, and honestly, babies are so tiny when they're first born, it always amazes me. Especially their little fingernails. Have you ever noticed how sharp newborn fingernails are? When I did my pediatric rotation in nursing school, I was absolutely terrified of clipping them. We had this one clinical instructor, Mrs. Gable, who was so incredibly strict about everything. If your scrubs were even slightly wrinkled, she'd send you home. She used to wear these bright red glasses... 

Oh, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um, but yeah, the muffin. I bought it, and I ate it in my car, and it was just... chewing. I didn't enjoy it at all. It just felt like a chore. So no, I don't really feel any pleasure from anything right now.
Do you feel guilty about anything in particular?

Um, guilt? No, not really. I don't think I have anything specific I feel guilty about. I mean, I guess I felt a little bad the other day because I forgot to water my roommate Sarah's plants. She has this huge Monstera plant right by our living room window. Have you seen those? The leaves get absolutely massive and they develop these natural splits and holes in them. People call it a Swiss cheese plant, which is kind of funny because I actually can't stand Swiss cheese. The taste is just too bitter or something. My dad used to always pack ham and Swiss sandwiches when we would go camping up at the lake. We had this old canvas tent that smelled exactly like wet dog, even though we didn't own a dog. My brother wanted a golden retriever so badly, but my mom was allergic to pet dander, so we ended up getting a hermit crab... 

Oh, gosh, I'm so sorry. My brain just keeps drifting off today. But um, no, I don't really feel guilty about anything. Just... just that heavy feeling I mentioned.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to be alive or hurting yourself?

Yeah, um... that's actually why I ended up saying something. I was at my prenatal appointment recently. The waiting room at my OB's office is always freezing, and they have the most outdated magazines. I was flipping through this home decor one from like four years ago, and it had this huge article on building a backyard fire pit. My roommate Sarah and I actually talked about getting one of those little portable ones for our patio, but our lease is super strict about open flames. Our landlord, Gary, is really intense about the rules. He’s the kind of guy who just shows up unannounced to check the gutters or the smoke detectors. And he always wears cargo shorts, even when it's literally freezing outside. I really don't understand how people can wear shorts in the winter. My legs get cold just walking from my car to the clinic for my shifts... 

Oh, gosh, sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. I'm sorry. Um, what I was trying to say was... at that prenatal appointment, I finally spoke up because I got really scared. I've been having these thoughts lately where I just... I kind of wish I just wouldn't wake up. I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that, I promise. It's just this heavy feeling of wanting to go to sleep and just not have to wake up and do it all over again.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, sad pressure?

It's been about three weeks. Yeah, it started shortly after I found out I was pregnant. I actually took the test in the staff restroom at the clinic during my lunch break. Which was probably a terrible idea because the lighting in there is just awful. They have those harsh fluorescent bulbs that buzz constantly and make everyone look kind of gray, you know? And the wall-mounted soap dispenser has been broken for months, so maintenance just left this giant pump bottle of cheap pink soap on the counter. It smells exactly like that artificial bubblegum flavor. Kind of like the liquid amoxicillin they give to kids? I always hated that smell. When I was little, I got strep throat like three times in one winter, and I had to take so much of that stuff. My mom would try to hide it by mixing it into my applesauce, but I could always tell because applesauce has that weird gritty texture if you really pay attention to it. We used to buy the big jars of it, but then my grandmother started making her own from the apple tree in her backyard... 

Oh, wow, I'm sorry. I'm doing it again. I don't know why I can't just stay on track today. But um, yeah, to answer your question... about three weeks. Ever since right after I found out about the baby.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or how quickly you're moving lately?

Yeah, um, my energy is just... gone. Everything I do feels really slowed down, almost like I'm moving through syrup. Even simple things at the clinic, like gathering wound care supplies or just finishing up my charting, it's taking me noticeably longer than it should. 

Speaking of charting, they actually just updated our electronic health record system last week, and it is a complete nightmare. They changed all the color codes for everything. The old system had patient allergies in bright red, which makes total sense, right? Red for danger. But now they're this weird pastel purple. Purple just reminds me of grape soda. I used to love grape soda when I was a kid. My grandpa would always buy those glass bottles of it from the corner store near his house. He had this old Ford pickup truck, and the seats were that sticky vinyl material that would absolutely burn the back of your legs in the summer if you were wearing shorts. We'd drive around with the windows down because the AC was broken, and his radio only ever picked up this one local country station that played the same five songs on a loop...

Oh, my goodness, I am so sorry. I'm doing it again. My brain is just everywhere. Um, but yeah, to answer your question, I just feel really sluggish. Like my body is just moving in slow motion lately.
Have you experienced any strange thoughts or heard any voices that others couldn't hear?

No, no, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or had any weird thoughts. It's just the sadness and feeling so tired. 

Honestly, the only thing I've been hearing lately is my roommate's new blender. Sarah bought this massive, industrial-grade blender last weekend because she decided she's going to get really into making smoothie bowls. The thing sounds like a jet engine taking off in our kitchen. She uses it at like six in the morning, too. I tried to tell her that the walls in our apartment are paper thin, but she insists she needs to blend her frozen kale right then. Kale is so tough to blend anyway. I tried growing kale once on the balcony of my old apartment, but these little green caterpillars completely decimated it in a matter of days. I think they were cabbage loopers? I spent an entire afternoon reading about organic pest control, trying to figure out how to make a garlic spray to keep them away. I ended up making my whole apartment smell like a pizzeria, and the caterpillars didn't even care. They just kept eating...

Oh, shoot. I'm sorry. I really don't know why I keep doing this today. But no, to answer your question, no voices or anything strange like that. Just the blender.
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still lately?

No, I haven't really felt restless. If anything, it's just the opposite, like I said, just feeling so slow and heavy. Sitting still is pretty much all I want to do right now. 

Actually, I spent most of yesterday just sitting on my couch watching this documentary about deep-sea diving. It's crazy how dark it gets down there, and the pressure is just immense. They were talking about these little submersibles they use, and how the windows have to be made of this special thick acrylic. Acrylic is such a weird material when you think about it. We used to use acrylic paints in my high school art class. Mr. Henderson, my art teacher, was obsessed with painting bowls of fruit. Like, every single week it was a new bowl of fruit. He had this fake plastic fruit that he'd arrange on a velvet cloth, but the plastic banana had this huge dent in it from where someone dropped it, and he refused to replace it. He said it added character. He was a funny guy, always wore these brightly patterned bow ties. I think he had a different one for every day of the month...

Ugh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry. My mind just keeps wandering off. But no, I'm not restless. I'm not having any trouble sitting still.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Well, I think I kind of mentioned it earlier, but yeah, I definitely feel like I'm moving a lot slower. Everything just takes so much effort. Even my speech feels a bit... sluggish, I guess. Like it takes me a minute to find the right words. 

Speaking of words, I was trying to do a crossword puzzle the other day to keep my mind sharp, you know? But the clues were so obscure. One was a five-letter word for a type of ancient Greek coin. Who knows that off the top of their head? My brother used to collect coins when we were little. He had this big, heavy album filled with quarters from all fifty states. He was so meticulous about it, always polishing them and organizing them by year. He got really upset once because I accidentally spent his rare 1976 Bicentennial quarter on a candy bar at the gas station. It was one of those Whatchamacallit bars, which honestly are highly underrated. They have that crispy rice layer and the peanut butter... I haven't had one of those in years. They used to sell them in the vending machine at my old nursing school, but the machine was always breaking down and stealing people's dollar bills...

Oh, wow. I'm sorry. I just went right off track again. But um, yes, to answer your question, I do feel like I'm moving and talking slower than I usually do.
Do you think you would enjoy things if you had the energy to do them?

I don't think so. I really don't think it's just the energy. Even when I try to think about doing things I used to love, it just feels so... pointless. Like, after my shifts at the clinic, I used to always paint, or I'd go to my yoga class, or sometimes even salsa dancing just to decompress. But lately, I just go straight home, sit on that same couch, and ignore all my texts because none of it feels worth the effort. It's like the color has been drained out of everything. 

Speaking of color, I bought these really expensive watercolor paints a few months ago. They're from this boutique brand in France that still grinds their own pigments by hand. The ultramarine blue is supposed to be incredible, made from real lapis lazuli, just like they did in the Renaissance. I read this whole book once about the history of the color blue. Did you know it was one of the last colors to have a word for it in most ancient languages? Homer used to describe the sea as "wine-dark" instead of blue in The Odyssey. I had to read The Odyssey in my freshman year lit class, and my professor was this really intense guy who would pace back and forth across the front of the lecture hall, gesturing wildly. He actually tripped over a projector cord once and took down the whole screen with him. It made this massive crashing sound, and...

Oh, goodness. I'm sorry. I really can't seem to stay on topic today. But yeah, no, I don't think I'd enjoy those things right now, even if I wasn't so tired. I just don't care about them anymore.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in, even if it's just a little bit?

Honestly, no. Like I was just saying a second ago, all those things I used to do to decompress after my shifts—the painting, the yoga, the salsa dancing—I just don't have any interest in them anymore. I really just go home, sit on the couch, and ignore all my texts. 

I have so many unread messages right now. My friend Jenna keeps texting me pictures of her new puppy. It's a Golden Doodle, I think. People are so obsessed with those doodle mixes lately. Labradoodles, Bernedoodles... My aunt had a standard poodle when I was growing up, named Pierre. He was so incredibly smart, he actually figured out how to open doors by pulling down the handles with his paws. It was funny until he learned how to open the pantry and got into a five-pound bag of flour. He dragged it into the living room and it looked like a blizzard hit the house. My uncle had to get his heavy-duty shop vac from the garage to clean it up, and those things are so ridiculously loud. It sounded like a jet engine in the middle of our house. He used that vac for everything, though, even cleaning out his car... 

Oh, I'm so sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. But no, there isn't really anything I find pleasure in right now. Even a little bit. It's just easier to sit there and do nothing.
Do you feel like you're fidgeting or having trouble staying still when you're sitting or lying down?

Um, no, not fidgeting. Actually, it's the exact opposite, like I said before. Everything I do just feels so... slowed down. Like I'm moving through syrup all the time. Even really simple things at the clinic, like gathering wound supplies or just finishing up my charting, it all takes me noticeably longer than it should. 

Charting is the worst, honestly. We switched to this new electronic medical record system a few months ago, and everyone complains about it. It has so many unnecessary drop-down menus. I don't know who designs these things, but they clearly don't work in healthcare. My friend Sarah, who works in IT, told me once that software developers often build things based on theoretical models rather than practical application. She actually helped design a mobile app for tracking local food trucks. It was a pretty cool idea, you could see exactly where the taco truck or the crepe stand was parked in real time. I love a good crepe. There was this little place near my undergrad campus that made a savory crepe with goat cheese, spinach, and caramelized onions. It was amazing. I used to go there every Tuesday after my anatomy lab. Anatomy lab was so intense, the smell of formaldehyde would just linger on my clothes for days, no matter how many times I washed them. I tried using that fancy detergent with the essential oils, but...

Oh, gosh. I'm sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? But um, yeah, to answer your question, no, I'm not fidgety at all. I just feel incredibly slow and weighed down.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or restless when you're not doing anything?

I feel like I just answered that, but no, I'm really not restless or fidgety. It's totally the opposite. Like I was saying, everything I do just feels so slowed down. It's like I'm moving through syrup all the time. Even the most basic stuff at the clinic, like grabbing wound care supplies or trying to finish my charting, it takes me so much longer than it used to. 

Wound care can be so tedious anyway, especially when you have to pack a deep wound. We had this one patient a while back with a diabetic ulcer that just would not heal. We tried everything—different dressings, negative pressure therapy, you name it. He was this sweet older man who used to be a jazz musician. He played the saxophone, I think. Or maybe the trumpet? I can never remember the difference between the brass instruments. My cousin played the French horn in high school, and it was the weirdest looking thing, all coiled up like a snail shell. He had to carry it around in this massive hard case that was almost as big as he was. He was always a really small kid, kind of a late bloomer. His mom used to make him drink those protein shakes to try and help him grow, but they tasted like chalk and artificial chocolate. I hate anything artificial chocolate flavored. It always reminds me of those cheap advent calendars you get at the grocery store where the chocolate tastes like wax...

Sorry, I'm rambling again. But yeah, no fidgeting. Just feeling really, really slow.
Have you been wanting to be around other people or avoiding social interactions lately?

Um, I've definitely been avoiding people. I was mentioning earlier that I just ignore all my texts now, even from my close friends. I'm just pulling away from everyone and everything that usually keeps me steady. I'm still making it to work at the clinic, but barely. My supervisor actually pulled me aside the other day because she noticed my charting has been incomplete lately. 

I just can't focus on the charts. Like I said, that new electronic system is terrible. But honestly, even before the new system, charting was my least favorite part of nursing. When I was in nursing school, we had this instructor, Mrs. Gable, who was so incredibly strict about documentation. She used to say, "If you didn't chart it, it didn't happen." She wore these really thick glasses on a beaded chain around her neck, and she would peer over them at you if you missed even one checkmark. She reminded me so much of my middle school librarian, Mrs. Higgins. Mrs. Higgins was obsessed with the Dewey Decimal System. If you put a book back on the wrong shelf, she would somehow know it was you and track you down in the cafeteria. The cafeteria food in middle school was actually pretty decent, they had these amazing square pizzas on Fridays. The cheese would get all crispy around the edges...

Oh, sorry. I don't know why I keep doing that. But to answer your question, yes, I'm definitely avoiding social interactions. I just don't have the energy for people right now.
Do you find yourself pacing back and forth or feeling an inner restlessness when you're sitting still?

I feel like we just talked about this, but no, I'm not pacing or restless at all. It's the exact opposite, like I've been saying. Everything I do just feels so incredibly slowed down. It's like I'm moving through syrup, just to do the most basic things. Even at the clinic, just gathering wound supplies or trying to finish my charting, it takes me noticeably longer than it should. 

And I know I keep bringing up the charting, but it really is the worst. We have this one doctor, Dr. Aris, who is so particular about how the notes are formatted. He wants everything in this very specific order, and if you miss one little detail, he sends it back to you. He's a good doctor, I guess, but he has zero bedside manner. He actually wears these ridiculous bow ties every single day. I don't think I've ever seen him in a regular tie. My grandfather used to wear bow ties, but he was a professor of medieval history, so it kind of fit his whole vibe, you know? He had this massive library in his house, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves filled with these dusty old tomes. I used to love the smell of that room. It smelled like old paper and pipe tobacco. He smoked cherry pipe tobacco, which I know is terrible for you, but it smelled so sweet. I tried to find a candle that smelled like that once, but they all just smelled artificial, kind of like that cheap chocolate I was talking about earlier. It's so hard to find a good candle that actually smells like what it says it does. 

Oh, gosh. I'm sorry. I'm totally off track again. But yeah, no inner restlessness or pacing. Just feeling really, really slow and heavy.
Do you think your current state is the worst it's been, or have you felt this low before?

I'm honestly not sure if this is the absolute worst it's ever been. It's hard to compare, you know? It's just really bad right now. I've definitely felt down before, but this just feels so heavy. Like I said, everything is just so slow. It's like that feeling when you're trying to run in a dream and you just can't get your legs to move fast enough. 

I actually used to have this recurring dream when I was a kid where I was trying to run away from a giant wave, but my feet were stuck in the sand. We went to the beach every summer in North Carolina, the Outer Banks. The sand there gets so incredibly hot by mid-afternoon, you have to sprint from your towel to the water or your feet will literally blister. My brother actually got second-degree burns on his soles once because he refused to wear his flip-flops. He was always so stubborn. He’s an engineer now, building bridges or something out in Oregon. It rains so much out there. I don't think I could handle that much rain. I need the sun, even if I'm just sitting inside avoiding everyone right now. I used to love sitting out on the porch in the summer with a glass of iced tea, the real kind, brewed with lots of sugar, not that powdered stuff. The powdered stuff always clumps up at the bottom of the pitcher and you have to stir it forever...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right. Have I felt this low before? I don't know, maybe? It's just really awful right now.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling like you need to move when you're sitting still?

I know you just asked me this, or something really similar. But no, no fidgeting. It's really the complete opposite. Everything I do feels so slowed down. Like I'm moving through syrup. Even simple things at the clinic, like gathering wound supplies or finishing my charting, it takes me noticeably longer than it should. 

And wound care is usually my favorite part of the job, too. We use this specific type of silver-infused dressing for the really stubborn ones. It actually looks a lot like the foil wrappers on those little chocolate eggs they sell around Easter. I used to love finding those during the egg hunts my church put on. They always hid the golden egg somewhere impossible, like up in the gutters of the rectory. Father Thomas was the one who hid them, and he was surprisingly spry for a guy in his seventies. He used to ride this vintage Schwinn bicycle all over town. It was that classic robin's egg blue color. My first car was actually that same color, a hand-me-down Honda Civic. The AC was totally busted, so in the summer I'd have to roll all the windows down, and my hair would get so tangled it took half a bottle of conditioner just to brush it out... 

Sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? But no, no fidgeting. Just really, really slow.
Do you feel like you're at a point where you can't imagine feeling better, or is there a part of you that thinks things might improve?

I don't know about things improving. I just... I came in because for the past few weeks, I’ve felt this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me almost all day. Even when I’m at work, smiling at the patients and pretending everything is fine, inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together. It’s exhausting, honestly. 

Smiling takes so much energy. We have this one patient, Mrs. Gable, she comes in every Tuesday for her B12 shot, and she always brings us these homemade snickerdoodles. They are amazing, honestly, the perfect amount of cinnamon. My grandmother used to make snickerdoodles, but hers were always a little too hard. She baked them on this ancient, warped baking sheet that she refused to throw away. She said it seasoned the cookies, whatever that means. It was black with years of burnt sugar and grease. She kept it in the drawer under the oven, the one where everyone else keeps their extra pots and pans. I don't actually have that drawer in my apartment right now. The kitchen is so tiny, you can barely open the fridge all the way without hitting the counter. It’s one of those old buildings with the exposed brick, which looks cool, but it’s drafty in the winter. The heating bill was outrageous last January. I had to buy one of those space heaters that looks like a little fireplace. It even has fake flames that flicker... 

But yeah, I don't know if I can imagine feeling better. Right now, it's just that constant, heavy sadness all day long.
Do you think you're experiencing the worst episode of depression in your life right now?

I honestly don't know if it's the absolute worst. I mean, I'm just so tired and sad all the time right now, it's hard to even think about other times. It feels like the worst, but maybe that's just because I'm in it right now. It's kind of like when you have a terrible stomach bug and you swear you've never been that sick in your life, but really you just forgot how bad the last one was. 

I had norovirus a couple of years ago, caught it from my niece. She's in daycare, and those places are basically just petri dishes. They were making these little handprint turkeys for Thanksgiving, and she smeared paint all over my favorite sweater. It was this really soft cashmere blend I found at a thrift store for like, eight dollars. Such a steal. Thrift shopping is the best, you never know what you're going to find. I once found a complete set of vintage Pyrex mixing bowls, the ones with the primary colors. The yellow one is perfect for making potato salad. I always put celery seed in my potato salad, it's the secret ingredient. People always ask what makes it taste so different, and I just smile and tell them it's a family secret. My mom used to make it for every Fourth of July barbecue. We'd go to the park and watch the fireworks... 

I'm sorry, I forgot what we were talking about again. The worst depression? I'm just not sure. It's just really bad right now.
